title: The Coppergrave Warrens
story: The smelters of Coppergrave sank their spoil shaft the year the river turned green. They stopped digging when the shaft answered them back.

notes.text: A weighing room. The scales are gone but their iron cradles remain, and someone has stacked river stones in them to the exact weight of a child.
Slag heaps cooled into glassy black waves. Walking on them is loud, and the sound carries a long way down the shaft.
The barred store. Copper ingots stamped with a maker's mark nobody in the valley uses any more.
A tally room the smelters walled up. Chalk marks cover every surface, counting something past four thousand.
A round chamber under a corbelled dome. Speak here and the dome answers a half-beat late.
An orphan key with no room under it — the geometry never placed this one.
The narrow crawl opens into a drying floor. Racks of something that was never grain.
A second key dropped into the slag heaps, where key 1 already sits.
The spoil shaft itself: a straight fall of stairs cut for barrows, worn into a gutter down the middle.

ending: Whatever the Coppergrave dug for, it is still digging.
